facts.claim: Dubai's Tourism Dirham is a flat fee per occupied room per night set by hotel classification: five-star or higher AED 20, four-star AED 15, three-star AED 10, two-star AED 10, one-star or budget AED 7, hotel apartments AED 20 (luxury), 15 (deluxe), 10 (standard), guest house AED 7; it is not charged per person.

sources.title: Dubai Legislation Portal: Executive Council Resolution No. 2 of 2014 (Schedule 1)

articles/where-to-stay-in-dubai.html: a flat fee of AED 7 to AED 20 a room a night set by the hotel's category
charged per occupied room, per night, by the hotel's classification
It is per room, not per person, so two people sharing pay it once

facts.claim: The Tourism Dirham is charged for a maximum of 30 consecutive nights and is collected from the main guest occupying the room.

sources.title: Dubai Legislation Portal: Administrative Resolution No. 2 of 2020, Articles 2(1) and 4(a)

articles/where-to-stay-in-dubai.html: It is charged for a maximum of 30 consecutive nights, to the main guest in the room

facts.claim: Dubai Decree No. 27 of 2019 reduced the municipality fee on sales of hotel establishments from 10% to 7%; hotels' own October 2026 rate terms list a 7% municipality fee, a 10% service charge and 5% VAT per room per night. (The u.ae portal page still lists 10% municipality fees generically; the decree and the hotel terms both say 7% for Dubai.)
